Digital transformation involves the creation, modification or translation of existing business processes into digital form. This online self-paced course explores why digital transformation has become a business imperative and how to create a proper roadmap for it. Participants will learn to use a balanced scorecard as a management tool to measure success and enhance their ability to lead digital transformation initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·       recognizing the primary components of digital capability

·       identifying the core digital capabilities of digital transformation

·       sequencing the steps in creating a digital transformation roadmap

Digital Transformation Leadership.description_en:

This online self-paced course assembles a playbook of best practices for digital transformation that focus on the customer, mobilize operational processes and sustain the employee experience during a period of change. · identifying the four major components of implementing digital transformation

Agile Stakeholder Engagement.description_en:
The Agile method for project management works best when a project team is cohesive, productive and engaged, with a clear understanding of project requirements and stakeholder expectations. This online self-paced course offers insights into the characteristics of agile project teams and team leaders, and recommends strategies to help improve team performance and cohesion. Participants will learn about communication tools and developmental mastery models in Agile, as well as the benefits of using facilitation techniques like games to foster collaboration and cooperation.

Topics include:

- identifying strategies for achieving stakeholder commitment
- engaging stakeholders through the five phases of the Agile Project Management model
- reviewing decision-making techniques and tools
- describing the characteristics of a cohesive and effective team

This online self-paced course provides an overview for non-specialists of the materiel management functions and how they relate to the procurement and real property functions. Policy decisions are most likely to achieve their desired outcomes and instill public trust when they are informed by the best available evidence. This online self-paced course explores the process of defining, gathering and weighing evidence that is relevant to a policy decision. · weighing evidence to infer whether a claim is true or false, and determining the level of confidence with which this can be done

· acknowledging evidence gaps and the implications of changes to evidence over time

Departments and agencies use a variety of solicitation methods to acquire goods and services through competitive contracts. This course covers two critical elements of the solicitation process: the statement of work and the evaluation criteria for bids submitted. Participants will learn how to write proper requirements to obtain their desired product or service and how to set evaluation criteria that will help select the appropriate bidder.

Topics include:

• identifying the components of a proper statement of work
• understanding the implications of trade agreements
• defining the requirements of the contract
• assessing, managing and mitigating contract risks
• selecting a contractor

Notes:

To gain a better understanding of the subject matter, participants are strongly recommended to complete Overview of Procurement (COR403) or the combination of Procurement Fundamental (COR401) and The Procurement Process (COR402) before registering to COR407.

Cost/Benefit Evaluation within Digital C.title_en: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Application (FON203)
Cost/Benefit Evaluation within Digital C.description_en:
Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) is a structured approach used to identify and assess potential outcomes to better inform decisions. This course explores the intricacies of the CBA process and emphasizes how rigorous analysis is pivotal to supporting evidence-based decision-making, specifically by federal regulators. Participants will acquire the skills needed to conduct a basic CBA to support the creation of a regulatory impact analysis statement (RIAS).

Topics include:

•	revisiting the theoretical foundations of CBA •	building CBA models •	assessing potential positive and negative outcomes •	supporting quantitative, qualitative and monetizing analyses •	summarizing results and drafting recommendations for decision-makers

Notes:

To receive a certificate of completion, participants must attend two virtual instructor-led sessions over the course of two weeks. They must prepare for the instructor-led sessions by also completing five online self-paced modules:


1. Self-paced modules 1 and 2
2. Virtual instructor-led session 1 (week 1; 2.5 hours)
3. Self-paced modules 3, 4 and 5
4. Virtual instructor-led session 2 (week 2; 2.5 hours)

Learners who are unfamiliar with the basic concepts of cost-benefit analysis are highly encouraged to complete Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Introduction (FON202) before registering for this course.
Cost/Benefit Evaluation within Digital C.title_fr: Analyse coûts-avantages dans la réglementation fédérale : application (FON203)
Cost/Benefit Evaluation within Digital C.description_fr:
L'analyse coûts-avantages est une approche structurée servant à déterminer et à évaluer d'éventuels résultats afin de prendre des décisions éclairées. Ce cours porte sur les particularités de l'analyse coûts-avantages et met l'accent sur le fait qu'une analyse rigoureuse est essentielle à la prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes, en particulier dans la réglementation fédérale. Les participants acquerront les compétences nécessaires pour faire une analyse coûts-avantages de base qui servira à l'élaboration d'un résumé de l'étude d'impact de la réglementation.

Sujets traités :

•	revoir les notions de base de l'analyse coûts-avantages; •	créer des modèles d'analyse coûts-avantages; •	évaluer les résultats éventuellement négatifs et positifs d'un règlement; •	réaliser des analyses quantitatives, qualitatives et monétaires; •	résumer des résultats et rédiger des recommandations à l'intention des décideurs.

Remarques :

Pour obtenir un certificat d’achèvement, les participants doivent assister à deux séances virtuelles dirigées par un enseignant sur une période de deux semaines. Ils doivent par ailleurs se préparer aux séances virtuelles en suivant les cinq modules à rythme libre, selon l’ordre suivant :


1. Modules 1 et 2 à rythme libre
2. Séance 1 en salle de classe virtuelle dirigée par un enseignant (semaine 1; 2,5 heures)
3. Modules 3, 4 et 5 à rythme libre
4. Séance 2 en salle de classe virtuelle dirigée par un enseignant (semaine 2; 2,5 heures)

Les personnes qui ne connaissent pas les notions de base de l'analyse coûts-avantages sont fortement encouragées à suivre le cours Analyse coûts-avantages dans la réglementation fédérale : introduction (FON202) avant de s'inscrire à ce cours-ci.

Cross-Functional Digital Collaboration.description_en:
Effective project management requires project managers to properly define the roles and responsibilities of their project team. This online self-paced course explores the characteristics of core project roles, including the project manager, coordinator, sponsor, team member, subject matter expert and stakeholder. Participants will learn about the different roles and responsibilities involved in project management, including the differences between project management and project leadership.

 

Topics include:

- defining project management roles and outlining the responsibilities of each
- distinguishing between project management and project leadership
- reviewing the key characteristics of emotional intelligence in project management

 

Notes:

This course is intended for all public servants, including those with or without project management experience. Materials are aligned with the PMBOK® Guide – Seventh Edition.

Completion of the 26 courses in the CAPM® course series can count towards the eligibility requirements for the Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM®) exam administered for a fee by the Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
The CAPM® exam is not administered by the Canada School of Public Service. Learners wishing to take the exam are responsible for validating their eligibility directly with PMI.
Cross-Functional Digital Collaboration.title_fr: CAPM® : Rôles et responsabilités au sein du projet (TRN341)
Cross-Functional Digital Collaboration.description_fr:
Afin d'assurer une gestion de projet efficace, les gestionnaires de projet doivent définir adéquatement les rôles et responsabilités au sein de leur équipe. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre explore les caractéristiques des rôles fondamentaux liés à un projet, notamment la direction, la coordination, la promotion et les rôles de membre de l'équipe, d'expert métier et de partie prenante. Les participants en apprendront sur les rôles et responsabilités qui entrent en ligne de compte dans la gestion de projet, y compris les différences entre la gestion et le leadership.

 

Sujets traités :

- définir les rôles liés à la gestion de projet et présenter les responsabilités de chacune et chacun;
- faire la distinction entre la gestion de projet et le leadership d'un projet;
- examiner les principales caractéristiques de l'intelligence émotionnelle dans la gestion de projet.

 

Remarques :

Ce cours s'adresse à tous les fonctionnaires, qu'ils aient ou non de l'expérience en gestion de projet. Le matériel est conforme à la septième édition du Guide PMBOK®.

La réussite des 26 cours de série de cours CAPM® peut être prise en compte dans les conditions d’admissibilité à l’examen payant d’Associé certifié en gestion de projet (CAPM®) du Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
L’examen CAPM® n’est pas offert par l’École de la fonction publique du Canada. Les apprenants qui souhaitent le passer sont responsables de vérifier leur admissibilité directement auprès du PMI.

Metadata-Driven Concept Systems.description_en:
In a rapidly evolving technological landscape, public service leaders need a clear understanding of artificial intelligence (AI) to make sound decisions about its use and integration. This course provides executive teams the opportunity to advance their understanding of AI, its current capabilities, potential benefits, risks, and implementation across the Government of Canada. Participants will become better prepared to make informed decisions about the adoption of AI in their respective organizations. 

  

Topics include: 


understanding the core concepts of AI, including the relationship between data and AI 

- exploring AI use cases and lessons learned in the Government of Canada 


- enabling policy-compliant and responsible adoption of AI systems and tools


- navigating organizational readiness, data maturity, and governance of risk, ethics, and privacy 

  

Notes:

This course is presented in the form of a briefing and is reserved for government executives. Offerings are delivered upon request from departmental officials or secretariats, with their delivery coordinated in partnership with the Canada School of Public Service. Please contact your departmental training coordinator to inquire about scheduling a session for your department.

Exception Documentation and Digital Just.description_en:
As the world becomes increasingly digital, public service skill sets and service delivery must follow suit. This course provides a high-level overview of the Government of Canada Digital Standards, which constitute the cornerstone of the government's shift to digital and to becoming more agile, open and user-focused. Participants will consider the positive impacts of the government's digital standards on the everyday work of public servants and explore ways to adapt to new digital realities and mindsets.
 
Topics include:
 
·       understanding the current context and enablers of a digital government
·       defining the Government of Canada Digital Standards
·       recognizing digital behaviours in relation to the Digital Standards
·       applying the Digital Standards in the context of your work

Interpretation of Automated Data Source.title_en: Evidence-Informed Decision-Making: Weighing Evidence for Policy Decisions (TRN505)
Interpretation of Automated Data Source.description_en:
Policy decisions are most likely to achieve their desired outcomes and instill public trust when they are informed by the best available evidence. This online self-paced course explores the process of defining, gathering and weighing evidence that is relevant to a policy decision. Participants will learn why decision-makers and scientists may have different standards of proof for the same factual claim.


Topics include:

· recognizing biases that can skew the evidence on which a decision is based

· weighing evidence to infer whether a claim is true or false, and determining the level of confidence with which this can be done

· acknowledging evidence gaps and the implications of changes to evidence over time
